A home game console is a specialized game machine typically used with a television in a shared living-room space. Standardized hardware and controllers give designers a predictable performance and input target.

Console play often supports comfortable long sessions and local social play, but certification, proprietary development access, screen distance, and shared display conditions constrain interface and production choices.

A homogeneous element of a [[Graded Ring]] or graded module belongs to one degree component. Multiplying homogeneous elements adds their degrees.

Every element is a finite sum of homogeneous components. Homogeneous generators let ideals, modules, and resolutions be studied degree by degree rather than only as undifferentiated algebraic objects.

A homogeneous ideal is an ideal generated by [[Homogeneous Element]]s. Equivalently, whenever it contains an element, it contains each homogeneous component of that element.

Quotienting a [[Graded Ring]] by a homogeneous ideal preserves a grading. Extension and contraction along graded homomorphisms also preserve homogeneity under the source's conditions.

A homogeneous linear system has the form $Ax=0$. It always has the [[Trivial Solution]] $x=0$.

If the coefficient matrix lacks full column rank, the system also has infinitely many nontrivial solutions. The null space formed by all solutions is a [[Vector Subspace]].

A homography is a projective transformation that maps points on one plane to their corresponding positions in another image or plane. A square AR marker has known planar coordinates, so its four detected image corners provide enough constraints to estimate this mapping.

With a calibrated camera, the homography can be decomposed into a rotation and translation consistent with the marker plane. Noise makes the estimate approximate, which is why pose refinement may follow.

A hook binds selected vertices or control points to another object, commonly an Empty, through a Hook modifier. Transforming the controller then deforms the assigned points.

Hooks provide looser and more directional control than predefined shape keys. They are useful for broad organic deformation and for animating curve control points, and their influence can be adjusted in the modifier.

A horizon graph divides positive and negative deviations into magnitude bands, mirrors the negative bands, and overlays the bands within a compact strip. Hue distinguishes sign while color intensity distinguishes magnitude. This compression lets many time series appear as vertically aligned [[Time-Series Small Multiples]] without losing broad changes. Exact values are difficult to recover, so a horizon graph is best for pattern comparison rather than precise reading.

A horizon graph scale determines the magnitude boundaries mapped to successive color bands. A common scale supports comparison among panels because the same intensity means the same deviation everywhere. Panel-specific scales expose each series' internal variation but prevent direct magnitude comparison. The choice must match the question and be stated clearly, because the compact encoding of a [[Horizon Graph]] makes an unnoticed scale change especially misleading.

A horizontal bar chart rotates the categorical axis so labels read along rows. It is useful when category names are long or when ranked values should be scanned from top to bottom.

The bars still require a common quantitative baseline, clear units, and a deliberate ordering.

A horizontal business process supports many kinds of organizations without defining their industry-specific product. Payroll, human resources, billing, auditing, and training are examples of functions needed across different business models.

Commonality makes these processes strong candidates for standardization and [[Business Process as a Service]]. A provider can spread the cost of a repeatable workflow across consumers while exposing the interfaces each organization needs.

A Householder transformation is an orthogonal reflection of the form $H=I-2uu^T/(u^Tu)$. It maps a vector onto a chosen coordinate direction and can zero many entries at once.

Successive reflections reduce a symmetric matrix to tridiagonal form or a general matrix toward Hessenberg form, preparing it for a [[QR Algorithm]].

A Hovmoller diagram places time on one axis, a spatial coordinate or zone on the other, and an aggregated field value in color. It reduces one spatial dimension of a [[Space-Time Raster]], making propagation, seasonality, and persistent bands visible in a single panel. The aggregation direction and function must be stated because distinct geographic patterns can produce the same reduced matrix.

A hub connection is the client-side object that represents an active SignalR relationship with a hub endpoint. It is configured with the server URL, registers handlers for server messages, and is then started asynchronously.

The connection belongs to the lifetime of the UI behavior that consumes it. Setup and cleanup therefore need to be paired so navigation and rerendering do not create duplicate subscriptions.

A hub-and-spoke level layout uses a central, relatively safe area connected to several outward paths. Players leave the hub to pursue challenges and return after completing or abandoning them.

The hub provides orientation, recovery, services, and repeated social or narrative contact. Spokes can be unlocked or attempted in different orders while the stable center limits navigational complexity.

A human-on-a-chip is the proposed integration of multiple organ models into a connected system that reproduces important body-wide signaling and drug distribution. Fluid connections could reveal effects that appear only after one tissue transforms a compound used by another.

Major barriers include missing organ models, scaling relationships, and the lack of one culture medium that supports all tissues simultaneously.

A hybrid cloud combines two or more component clouds into a system with its own useful characteristics. The components may use public, private, or community deployment models and may expose different service abstraction levels.

The components normally need to share data, processes, or control. A hybrid design can keep sensitive work in a [[Private Cloud]] while using standard public services for flexibility, or can duplicate a service in another cloud for continuity and [[Cloud Bursting]].

A hybrid feature-selection method combines a fast filter with a clustering-aware refinement. The filter narrows the candidate set, and a wrapper or embedded stage then tests how the surviving features affect cluster structure.

This design reduces the search cost of a pure wrapper while retaining more task sensitivity than a standalone filter. Its result depends on both stages, so the filtering threshold must not discard dimensions that become useful only in combination.

A hybrid mobile application places a responsive web application inside a native container. HTML, CSS, and JavaScript can provide one shared interface implementation, while the container supplies installation and selected access to device capabilities.

This approach reduces duplicated UI work but introduces a web rendering layer between the application and native controls. Performance, interaction fidelity, and access to platform features therefore depend on the container and its native bridges.

A hybrid random walk moves within user or item domains and across user-item links in a star-structured graph. Steady-state probabilities estimate user tie strength, item relevance, and the likelihood of adoption or rejection.

Updates combine routes through similar users, similar items, labels, and observed cross-domain behaviors. This transfers auxiliary knowledge into a target recommendation while addressing [[Behavioral Data Sparsity]] and the [[Cold-Start Problem]].

A hybrid recommender system combines collaborative and content-based information so one approach can compensate for weaknesses in the other. Item features can support new or sparsely rated items, while collective behavior can reveal preferences not obvious from content alone.

The combination may occur through blended scores, staged models, or shared representations. Evaluation must show that added complexity improves useful recommendations rather than only fitting historical interactions.

A hybrid warehouse places frequently used data in a conventional warehouse while storing larger, older, or less frequently accessed collections in distributed storage. A connection between the environments can present a unified query interface and combine results computed in each location.

The architecture responds to different cost and latency needs rather than declaring one storage system universally superior. Its usefulness depends on whether data meaning, access rights, query execution, and result integration remain coherent across the two places.

A hydroelectric plant stores water at height and conducts it through penstocks toward a turbine. Water's potential energy becomes directed flow and turbine rotation, which drives an electrical generator. The source notes that the arrangement depends on a suitable site and water resource and can require a dam. It has a mechanical conversion stage despite using renewable input energy.

A hydrogel is a water-rich polymer network whose soft mechanical behavior can resemble biological tissue. Cells can be embedded while the material is liquid and retained when physical, thermal, chemical, or light-driven crosslinking turns it into a gel.

Natural hydrogels carry biological signals; synthetic hydrogels offer tighter control over stiffness, chemistry, and degradation.

A hydrogen fuel-cell vehicle feeds stored hydrogen to a [[Fuel Cell]] and uses its electrical output to drive a propulsion motor. It differs from a [[Hydrogen Combustion Vehicle]], which burns fuel to move an engine piston or turbine. The source presents polymer-membrane cells as suitable for transport because output can change quickly, while fuel storage and distribution remain system-level constraints.

A hydrogen-combustion vehicle burns hydrogen with air in an engine rather than turning it into electricity in a [[Fuel Cell]]. The source describes manifold mixing or direct injection and altered spark timing because hydrogen flames travel rapidly. Water is the fuel's carbon-free combustion product, but hot air combustion can still form nitrogen oxides. On-board gas or hydride storage adds volume or weight constraints.

A hydrogen-fired plant burns hydrogen to heat a gas or steam power cycle, rather than using a [[Fuel Cell]] for direct electrochemical output. The source considers central combined-cycle and cogeneration arrangements, but also notes hydrogen's faster flame and higher flame temperature can destabilize combustion and raise nitrogen-oxide emissions. Plant equipment and controls must therefore be evaluated for the fuel, not assumed interchangeable with natural gas.

A hydrogen-oxygen [[Fuel Cell]] combines hydrogen with oxygen to produce water and electrical work. Hydrogen loses electrons at one electrode, and the external circuit carries them to the oxygen-side reaction; ions move through the [[Fuel Cell Electrolyte]] to maintain charge balance. For one mole of hydrogen consumed, the ideal reaction produces one mole of water. Real output is below the reversible limit because of polarization losses.

A hyperbolic network embedding assigns coordinates in [[Hyperbolic Space]] to graph nodes. One approach approximates observed graph distances, while another chooses coordinates that make the observed network likely under a hyperbolic growth model.

Once embedded, coordinate distance can accelerate shortest-path estimates, centrality calculations, missing-link prediction, routing, and visualization. The value of the embedding depends on both its computational cost and its structural distortion.

A hyperbolic radial fin varies its thickness along a profile defined by a hyperbolic relationship and extends around a central axis. The profile can be parameterized in a work plane and revolved to create the three-dimensional solid.

The changing thickness redistributes material between the base and outer radius. Profile continuity, minimum thickness, volume, and surface measurements are necessary checks before comparing the design with constant-thickness radial fins.

A hypergraph edge can connect more than two vertices, preserving multiway relationships that an ordinary graph would decompose into pairwise links. Hypergraph partitioning divides vertices while minimizing cut hyperedges under balance constraints.

This representation is useful for transactions, circuits, and relational data in which one event joins many objects. The cut definition must specify whether splitting a hyperedge once or across several blocks carries different cost.

A hyperlink is a reference from text to another location in the same document or to a different document. On the web, a hyperlink creates a directed connection from its source page to its destination page.

These connections turn pages into a [[Web Graph]]. Incoming links become [[Backlink|backlinks]], and PageRank treats each outgoing link as receiving part of the source page's relative importance.

A hyperlink matrix normalizes an [[Adjacency Matrix]] by dividing each nonzero entry in a row by the number of outgoing links represented in that row. Every linked destination thereby receives an equal share of the source page's importance.

Multiplying the [[PageRank Vector]] by this matrix redistributes rank through the [[Web Graph]]. Rows of zeros created by pages with no outgoing links require correction before the [[Power Method]] can produce a reliable ranking.

A hypernetwork generalizes an ordinary graph by allowing one hyperlink to connect more than two nodes. The network is defined by a node set and a family of nonempty node subsets that serve as its hyperlinks.

This representation is useful when a relationship belongs to a group as a whole rather than decomposing naturally into independent pairs. Pairwise projection can lose that joint structure.

A hyperparameter is a modeling choice set outside the ordinary parameter-fitting step. The neighbor count in [[K-Nearest Neighbors]], the span in LOESS, and the number of retained dimensions are examples that control flexibility or representation.

Choosing the value by minimizing training error creates optimistic bias. [[Cross-Validation]] estimates performance on held-out folds so competing hyperparameters can be compared without using the final test set for tuning.

Kelleher contrasts manually fixed neural-network choices with weights fitted during training. The selected [[Activation Function|activation function]], [[Convolutional Stride|convolution stride]], and [[Learning Rate|learning rate]] are examples of choices that shape the training procedure or architecture rather than being adjusted by the ordinary parameter update.

The book tunes decision-tree complexity and loss choices by comparing held-out behavior, and it controls ensemble capacity through settings such as feature sampling, tree count, depth, learning rate, and boosting rounds. These choices shape the fitted procedure without being ordinary learned coefficients.

A JavaScript source map records how generated JavaScript corresponds to the original source from which it was compiled or bundled. It lets a debugger display and pause in [[TypeScript]] even though the browser executes JavaScript.

Without the mapping, client faults point only into transformed output that can differ substantially from the authored component or service. Source maps are therefore a development aid and should be handled according to deployment needs.

A jellyfish-inspired robot reproduces the body geometry and circumferential muscle organization that generate propulsive swimming in a jellyfish. Cardiomyocytes arranged on a flexible synthetic film contract synchronously and bend its lobes.

The example demonstrates that biological architecture can guide engineering alongside the direct use of biological material.

A job is a task that someone considers valuable, and computational design asks how a computer might help perform it. Framing value in terms of jobs keeps attention on what a user or community is trying to accomplish rather than on computation for its own sake.

Some jobs are well-defined enough for [[Automation]], while others involve concerns that cannot be reduced to fixed procedures. Computational thinking can still assist the latter through models, tools, and informed human-computer interaction.

A joint probability distribution assigns probabilities to combinations of values across several variables. It represents every probabilistic relationship the description makes available and is normalized over the full joint state space.

Bayesian programs rarely store an unrestricted joint table. They decompose it into smaller conditional factors using justified independence assumptions, then reconstruct the terms required for a particular question.

A journal Table 1 summarizes the analytic sample and the distribution of exposures and candidate confounders. For a categorical outcome it commonly reports frequencies and proportions overall and by outcome group; for a continuous outcome it commonly adds group means and standard deviations.

Bivariate test results may help readers understand group differences. The table should be generated from analysis objects or structured data whenever possible, because manually copying values from console output into a spreadsheet creates avoidable transcription risk.

A JPEG compression artifact is visible distortion caused by blockwise transformation, chroma reduction, and coefficient quantization rather than by scene content. Strong compression can create 8-by-8 blocking, ringing around sharp edges, color smearing, and loss of fine texture.

These patterns are often mistaken for evidence of editing. A forensic analyst should first determine whether an alleged anomaly is a normal consequence of the file's quality and repeated saves; only spatially or historically inconsistent artifacts support a tampering hypothesis.

A JPEG ghost is a regional difference pattern that appears when an already compressed image is recompressed across a range of candidate qualities. Pixels originating from a previous JPEG save respond differently near their earlier quality level than pixels with another compression history.

Mapping average absolute differences can reveal a pasted region whose effective quality differs from its surroundings. The result indicates inconsistent prior compression, not the exact editing operation, and naturally mixed or repeatedly processed files can complicate interpretation.

A JPEG quantization table signature uses the values that control how strongly spatial-frequency coefficients are rounded during compression. A color JPEG can contain three 8-by-8 tables—one for luminance and two for chrominance—providing 192 values whose pattern may be distinctive to a device or application.

Comparing those values with known outputs can identify an incompatible encoder or prior resave. Attribution remains probabilistic because different products can share tables and some cameras select tables dynamically according to scene or quality settings.

A JPEG recompression probe repeatedly saves a test image at candidate quality settings and measures the pixel difference between each result and the original file. A region previously encoded at one of those settings can show an anomalously small or structured difference near the matching quality.

Comparing the difference maps across qualities is the operational basis of [[JPEG Ghost]] analysis. The probe must preserve relevant alignment and encoding conditions, and it should be treated as a test of compression history rather than direct proof of compositing.

A JPEG signature is a collection of encoding choices that can characterize a camera or software pipeline. Quantization tables, embedded-thumbnail properties, and the order and contents of marker segments are particularly useful because different devices and applications package JPEG data differently.

A mismatch between a file's signature and its claimed source suggests that the image was resaved or did not come directly from that pipeline. A match is not proof of origin, since signatures can be shared, copied, or changed by firmware and export settings.

A JSON Web Token is a compact token format used to carry signed claims between an issuer and a client or API. Its signature allows the recipient to detect alteration and validate the issuing authority.

In a single-page application, IdentityServer can issue a JWT after authentication and the client can present it on API requests. The token is evidence to validate, not permission by itself; [[Authorization]] still evaluates the claims against an operation's policy.

A k-gram sequence feature represents an ordered contiguous pattern of exactly k elements. Its value may indicate presence, count occurrences, or weight the pattern within a sequence.

Increasing k captures more context but expands the candidate space and makes individual patterns rarer. Support constraints and feature selection help control this combinatorial growth.

A K-nearest-neighbor outlier has an unusually large distance to its kth nearest neighbor or an unusually large sum of distances to its k nearest neighbors. The score ranks observations by local isolation.

The choice of k defines the neighborhood scale. Computing all pairwise distances is expensive, so randomized ordering and pruning can reduce work.

A K-partite graph divides its vertices into K sets and permits edges only between different sets. In categorical clustering, the sets can represent attribute domains and vertices their values.

A clique selects mutually connected values across the parts. CLICK uses maximal supported cliques to describe combinations that form categorical clusters.

A K-prototypes center contains numeric means for continuous attributes and categorical modes for discrete attributes. The Kprototype class reuses the Kmean lifecycle but overrides center updating so each schema component receives the correct representative.

This inheritance is possible because assignment and iteration structure remain similar. The subclass also relaxes Kmean's numeric-only dataset validation to admit categorical and mixed records.

A kable table converts a data frame or matrix into a simply formatted table for a knitr report. It is useful when the underlying result is already organized and needs a readable presentation rather than complex styling.

Labels, units, rounding, and captions should be chosen deliberately instead of exposing raw object names.

A Kalman filter is a Bayesian filter specialized to linear state transitions and observations with Gaussian uncertainty. Those assumptions allow the belief state to be represented by a mean and covariance and updated analytically.

The prediction step propagates both the estimate and its uncertainty, while the correction step balances that prediction against a measurement. The relative covariances determine how strongly each source influences the posterior.

A Kanban board maps work items across columns that represent workflow states. Cards and queues reveal where work is active, waiting, blocked, or completed, allowing a team to inspect the entire flow at a glance.

The board should reflect the real process rather than an idealized one. Dates, buffers, and work limits can be added when they help measure [[Cycle Time]] or expose a [[Bottleneck]].

A key performance indicator is a selected measure used to judge whether a product change advances an important outcome, such as participation or retention. It turns a product hypothesis into evidence that can be observed after deployment.

A KPI is a proxy, not the purpose of the game. Optimizing a short-term number without context can harm player value or hide delayed effects, so metrics require interpretation and multiple forms of feedback.

A keyer may produce a useful alpha while degrading the RGB colors at the same time. Instead of taking both outputs unquestioningly, use the extracted matte to cut the subject from the original, pristine foreground footage. This separates the question of where the subject is visible from the question of what its pixels should look like. Spill and color corrections can then be applied deliberately. The book demonstrates this again in its stereo-conversion example after a blue-screen extraction. See [[Alpha Channel as Compositing Matte]] and [[Suppressing Chroma Spill]].

A keyframe records a property's value at a particular frame. Creating another keyframe for the same property at a later time gives Blender two important states between which it can calculate change.

Keys can be inserted from the 3D Viewport or directly from many interface properties. They establish the poses or values the artist chooses; interpolation determines what happens between them.

A keying background need not be blue or green. Its color should contrast clearly with the subject's colors so the keyer can separate them, and it should be saturated and lit as evenly as the shoot permits. A costume or object that repeats the screen color is likely to disappear with it. Uneven illumination expands the background's color range and forces a wider key tolerance, increasing the chance that foreground detail is lost. The screen choice therefore shapes the difficulty of the later [[Color-Space Keyer Tolerance]] adjustment.

A keying set groups properties that should receive keyframes together. Built-in sets such as location, rotation, and scale reduce the chance that one related channel will be overlooked.

Custom keying sets can coordinate properties spread across objects, constraints, materials, and other editors. They are especially useful for complex rigs whose animation controls would otherwise require many separate keying actions.

A kind of computation that can be derived from a premise and lead into a conclusion

A formal sequence of justified deductions is a proof.

More precisely, deduction preserves truth from accepted [[Premise|premises]] to a [[Conclusion]]. Rules such as [[Modus Ponens]] can be chained into a formal proof, where each line is either a premise or follows logically from earlier lines.

A Kmean iteration updates centers from current memberships and then reassigns every record to the closest center under the configured distance. The loop continues until no membership changes or the maximum iteration count is exceeded.

The assignment count supplies a direct convergence test, while the final squared-error objective summarizes compactness. Empty clusters require explicit handling because their centers cannot be updated from member averages.

A knitr chunk label gives an executable block a unique, meaningful identifier. Labels support caching, figure filenames, cross-reference workflows, and readable error messages.

A knitr code chunk is a delimited block of executable code inside a literate document. Chunk options control evaluation, display, caching, figures, and other output behavior.

A Kubernetes deployment declares how an application workload should run, including its image, labels, container settings, and desired replicas. Applying the YAML definition asks the cluster to bring its current state into agreement with that declaration.

The sales-order deployment refers to the image stored in Azure Container Registry and exposes its replica count as configuration. Updating the file and applying it provides a repeatable scale or rollout operation.

A Kubernetes node is a machine in the cluster that supplies compute resources for pods. The orchestrator selects nodes when placing workloads and can distribute replicas across the available capacity.

Nodes are infrastructure beneath the application's pods, not copies of the application themselves. Managed Kubernetes reduces direct machine administration, but node count and size still shape capacity and cost.

A Kubernetes pod is the workload unit in which one or more closely related containers run. The sales-order deployment produces worker pods from the registered Docker image, and each pod can independently draw messages from the shared queue.

Pods are replaceable rather than durable identities. When one is deleted, the deployment controller creates another so the requested replica count is restored.

A Kubernetes replica is one desired copy of a pod managed by a workload controller. Increasing the replica count permits more instances of a scalable worker to run; reducing it removes excess instances.

The book changes the sales-order deployment from two replicas to three and reapplies the manifest. Replication improves throughput and availability only because queued work prevents every instance from processing the same input indiscriminately.

A Lagrange basis polynomial for node $x_i$ is $L_i(x)=\prod_{k\ne i}(x-x_k)/(x_i-x_k)$. It equals one at $x_i$ and zero at every other interpolation node.

These selector properties make the weighted sum in [[Lagrange Interpolation]] reproduce every supplied function value while remaining a polynomial of the required degree.

A lambda expression is a compact anonymous function commonly supplied to LINQ operators as a predicate, selector, key function, or accumulator. Its parameters represent items flowing through the query, and its body describes the operation to apply.

The same syntax may compile to a delegate for in-memory execution or to an expression tree for provider translation. That contextual conversion is central to LINQ's ability to present one query style across very different data sources.

The inventory example passes a lambda as a product-price criterion to a filtering operation. The filtering mechanism remains unchanged while the lambda expresses the caller's selected business rule, illustrating a functional form of strategy selection.

A laminar flow model assumes orderly viscous motion without resolving turbulent fluctuations. For internal pipe flow, Reynolds number compares inertia with viscosity and provides a regime check; the book's pipe examples keep the value below about 2,300.

Because density and viscosity may vary with temperature and pressure, a velocity that begins in the laminar range may not remain there throughout a heated system. [[Thermal Model Verification and Sensitivity|sensitivity checks]] should therefore examine the regime criterion across the solved property range.

A landmark is an easily distinguishable object used to maintain spatial orientation, estimate distance or direction, and build landmark and route knowledge.

A global landmark is visible from much of the environment and supplies broad directional guidance. A local landmark supports decisions at a particular point. Effective landmarks are placed where they can be noticed and are visually distinct in color, texture, lighting, shape, or size.

Landmarks make environments more legible and support [[Wayfinding]], [[Spatial Knowledge]], and the construction of a [[Cognitive Map]].

An AR navigation system can highlight a physical landmark or attach a decision cue to it, connecting digital route information to a feature the traveler can recognize without the display. Stable real-world referents also help relate egocentric guidance to an exocentric overview.

A language is Turing-acceptable when some [[Turing Machine]] halts exactly on the strings in the language. For a string outside the language, the machine may run forever rather than halt with an explicit rejection.

Every [[Turing-Decidable Language|decidable language]] is acceptable, but the converse fails. Turing-acceptable languages are exactly the [[Recursively Enumerable Language|recursively enumerable languages]] and exactly the languages generated by general grammars.

A language is Turing-decidable when a [[Turing Machine]] computes its characteristic function: it halts on every input with 1 for membership and 0 for nonmembership. The requirement to halt in both cases distinguishes decision from mere acceptance.

Turing-decidable languages are also called [[Recursive Language|recursive languages]]. A language is decidable exactly when both it and its complement are [[Turing-Acceptable Language|Turing-acceptable]].

A lapse rate describes how temperature changes with altitude. Comparing the environmental lapse rate with the dry or saturated adiabatic response of a displaced parcel indicates whether the parcel tends to return, remain neutral, or continue rising. Potential-temperature gradients and measures such as convective available potential energy extend this comparison in [[Thermodynamic Weather Diagrams]].

A latent factor model represents users and items through a smaller set of learned dimensions that explain patterns in their interactions. The dimensions are not required to correspond directly to named attributes.

A preference score is produced from the relationship between a user's factors and an item's factors. This compact representation makes large sparse matrices more tractable while preserving the regularities most useful for prediction.

A latent semantic representation maps observed words and documents into hidden dimensions intended to capture recurring concepts or topics. Matrix factorization and probabilistic topic models reduce sparse vocabulary space by explaining co-occurrence through a smaller set of latent factors.

The representation can connect documents that discuss similar ideas with different words and reduce noise from synonymy or sparse counts. Its dimensions are learned from the corpus, so their stability and interpretation depend on the model, data, and chosen dimensionality.

A latent variable is included in a probabilistic description but is not directly observed in the available dataset or current question. It represents hidden structure that can explain dependencies, classes, states, or model choices among observed variables.

Inference assigns a distribution to the latent alternatives or marginalizes them. Learning with latent variables is an incomplete-data problem because parameter estimation must account for values that were not recorded.

A latitude nut applies a deliberate real-wander tendency that opposes the expected apparent drift from Earth's rotation at a selected latitude. The adjustment can make a directional gyro accurate in that region but becomes imperfect after substantial north-south travel. It is one term in the broader error budget described by [[Earth-Rate and Transport Wander]].

A lattice object is a coarse three-dimensional control cage used to deform another object. Moving a small number of lattice points produces a smooth change across the target without editing its dense topology directly.

The lattice is a control object rather than rendered surface geometry. It is useful for broad proportion changes and reusable deformations, after which the relationship can remain adjustable or be applied before an export pipeline that cannot represent it.

A law of formation is a rule that generates the members of a pattern or [[Sequence]]. It can describe how to obtain each term from earlier terms or give a direct formula from the term's position.

For (2,7,12,17,\ldots), the recursive law adds five each time, while the direct law gives the (n)th term as (2+5(n-1)). A proposed law should reproduce every listed case and specify which positions are allowed. Algebraic notation makes the rule reusable without enumerating the infinitely many terms it can generate.
